questions.prompt: What schedule should the Kaggle manager target?
questions.description: The request says daily snapshots; the current repo docs mention a more frequent example cadence. This decides the default schedule language and verification target.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use one full daily run as the default target, with the exact cron documented clearly. Avoid implying multiple daily versions unless intentionally selected.

questions.prompt: How far should the execution go once the implementation is ready?
questions.description: Kaggle dataset versioning is a live, credentialed action. This determines whether the plan should include an actual dataset/kernel push when local checks pass.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use configured Kaggle CLI credentials to create or version the public dataset and push the connected manager notebook, then verify the live dataset contents and metadata.

questions.prompt: What should block a dataset version from being published?
questions.description: The full sync touches public third-party job boards; transient 429s, 404s, and provider-specific failures can occur even when the pipeline is structurally correct.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Block on CLI crashes, schema/export/metadata validation failures, missing required artifacts, or an empty unusable snapshot; tolerate provider-level failures only when they are captured in metrics/provider error details and the dataset remains internally consistent.

questions.prompt: What verification should be required before calling the goal done?
questions.description: The repo has local unit/integration/docs/OpenSpec gates and Kaggle has live file/version surfaces. This chooses the expected assurance bar.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require generated-artifact parity, focused Kaggle metadata/export tests, full repo CI parity if feasible, a live Kaggle CLI create/version or dry-run-equivalent depending on deployment scope, and post-deploy checks for SQLite, CSV, Parquet, datapackage, dataset metadata, and manager notebook availability.
